claims.claim: Version-2 HUMAN_ON_DEMAND policy defines direct TASK/REPAIR/REMEDIATION defaults and soft AOA with explicit opt-out, distinct from historical approvals.
Ordinary TASK authoring supports a direct final candidate without audit stages or audit-source collection, retaining final contract validation.
Direct repair proposals retain failed-RUN/SHA, task, action, scope and constraint validation without mandatory ROA or Human audit-selection credentials.
Canonical remediation selection supports DIRECT while retaining exact finding, reviewed SHA, scope, verification and constraint checks.
Authenticated on-demand TCA binds one request to the exact canonical TASK revision/source and does not persist into later authoring attempts.
Authenticated subject-bound ROA and MOA remain callable on demand without becoming defaults or granting correction mutation authority.
AOA remains the soft architecture default; authenticated NO_AOA yields DIRECT, and explicit supported V1 selection remains subject-bound.
Forged, stale, partial and conflicting choices fail closed; publication validation errors become BrainContextError, while direct authoring requires no audit inputs.
Historical profile identities and archived stage/return interpretation remain intact, with rejection of in-flight audit reselection.
Planning records and contracts describe direct defaults and exact on-demand audits, preserve TASK-407 lineage, and suspend prospective R4 activation.
Positive and negative regressions cover direct paths, on-demand audits, AOA/V1 choices, stale inputs, historical modes and repaired publication. All 156 selected implementation-local cases passed.

Activation requires RUN-408-002's exact admitted repair lineage, genuine Runtime proof, independent PRIMARY REVIEW PASS and published source. Executor, ingress, scope and verification authority boundaries remain intact.
